facts: In February 1945, with the war in Europe nearly won, Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met at Yalta, in Crimea. They agreed to divide Germany into occupation zones and to found the United Nations. Stalin promised free elections in Poland and to join the war against Japan. Poland's borders moved west. Critics said the deal handed Eastern Europe to Stalin. Roosevelt died two months later, and Poland's elections in 1947 were rigged.

lines.say: In February 1945, with the war nearly won, President Roosevelt flew to Yalta, in Crimea, to meet Churchill and Stalin.
The Big Three sat down to decide the world after the war.
They agreed to divide Germany into zones, and to found the United Nations.
Stalin promised free elections in Poland, and to join the war against Japan.
Poland's borders moved west. Critics said the deal handed Eastern Europe to Stalin.
